messages:
customer-jamie: Hey team — after upgrading to @redwood/sdk@0.24.0 our calls to chat.create started returning 404 / route_not_found. Rolling back to 0.23.5 fixes it. Can you help?

emily-support: Sorry you're hitting that, Jamie. Can you paste the minimal repro (TS/Node snippet) and the exact error response body? Also include SDK version from package.json and the Authorization header pattern (no tokens please).

customer-jamie: Repro below (sanitized):
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.chat.create({
  model: 'redwood-1',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }]
});
```
Error: 404 {"error":"route_not_found","message":"no route for chat.create"}
SDK: 0.24.0
We also see this in prod logs: request_id=abc123, time=2026-03-10T17:05:12Z

marco-eng: Thanks — quick thought: we rolled out a small API path normalization change in the hosted control plane last week (it affects certain SDK path builders). SDK 0.24.0 included a new client-side router change that changed endpoint naming for streaming vs non-streaming calls. Looks like chat.create is being emitted as chat.createStream in some code paths. Can you run a packet/snippet that prints the outgoing URL? e.g. set RW_DEBUG=1

customer-jamie: With RW_DEBUG=1 I see POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/createStream in the request (but our org only has the non-stream /v1/chat/create route enabled).

emily-support: That helps. Two separate issues to resolve: 1) endpoint name mismatch (SDK emitting createStream) 2) retry/idempotency causing duplicated billing on retries (if retries happen after uncertain failures). Did you observe duplicate token billing for the same request?

customer-jamie: Yes — during a spike we saw 2 identical successful completions for the same user prompt within ~10s, both billed. We use our own retry wrapper around the SDK with axios-retry.

sre-liz: FYI — cross-checking request_id=abc123, I can see two server-side completes: abc123 and abc123-dup in the logs. Looks like the client retried without an Idempotency-Key, so the service treated it as a separate invocation. We typically recommend sending an Idempotency-Key header for at-least-once network retries.

marco-eng: Confirming a bug: SDK 0.24.0 changed the default header passthrough and accidentally dropped custom headers set on the client instance when it rewrites the path for stream vs non-stream. That caused two things: it picked the wrong path name in some code paths, and it dropped Idempotency-Key when users attached it to the wrapper headers. We have a PR queued to fix both behaviors.

emily-support: Workarounds for now: 1) pin to @redwood/sdk@0.23.5 2) if you must stay on 0.24.0, call the raw HTTP endpoint and set Idempotency-Key yourself:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/create" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $SOME_UUID" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
This will avoid the SDK path normalization and ensure idempotency.

customer-jamie: Appreciate that. For billing I need the duplicate charge refunded — can you open an incident? The two charges were ~1200 tokens each under org-id=org-789.

sre-liz: I've opened INC-2026 and added the request IDs and ingress timestamps. We'll review billing and refund duplicates if confirmed. Please send any additional request IDs or timestamps.

customer-jamie: Another datapoint — we inject a header X-Client-Version in our requests. With 0.24.0 I see that header missing in some requests, which made tracing harder.

marco-eng: Yep that's part of the same header-passthrough regression. The fix (PR #4251) restores propagation of user-specified headers and corrects path naming logic. I can attach a patched build if you want to test quickly (tgz).

customer-jamie: Would love the patched tgz for quick verification before we roll back.

emily-support: Sending via DM a link to the patched package and a short diff summary. Steps to test quickly: 1) npm i /path/to/@redwood-sdk-0.24.0-patch.tgz 2) run the minimal snippet with RW_DEBUG=1 and include an Idempotency-Key 3) confirm outgoing URL is /v1/chat/create and headers include Idempotency-Key + X-Client-Version.

marco-eng: I'll keep the PR high-priority. ETA for full npm publish: ~24–48h after verification. Thanks for the repro and logs, Jamie.

customer-jamie: Verified patched tgz — outgoing URL now /v1/chat/create and headers intact. No duplicate billing on retry when Idempotency-Key set. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

emily-support: Great — we'll follow up once the npm release is out and confirm refund status on INC-2026. If anything else pops up ping @emily-support or @sre-liz.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Notifying: rolling patch release queued for @redwood/sdk to staging (release/patch-0.24.1) — 1 changed file.

marco-eng: Follow-up action items: (1) publish 0.24.1 that restores header passthrough and path behavior (2) add unit + integration tests for custom header passthrough and idempotency header preservation (3) update changelog calling out idempotency guidance.

sre-liz: Billing update will be posted to INC-2026 within 48h. Closing thread here but keep adding logs to INC-2026 if you find more request IDs.

customer-jamie: Will do — thanks all!
